paper.citation: Athey, S., Imbens, G. W. and Wager, S. (2018). Approximate residual balancing: Debiased inference of average treatment effects in high dimensions. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Statistical Methodology), 80(4), 597–623. DOI: 10.1111/rssb.12268.
paper.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Statistical Methodology)
paper.source_locator: Section 5.2 “Simulation designs”, unnumbered many-cluster layout paragraph, printed pp. 616–617; article PDF reader pp. 20–21 of 27 (zero-based page indices 19–20). Table 2 and its footnote on printed p. 617 specify n=800, p=4000, ||beta||_2=3 and 400 replications. No source equation number is assigned to the DGP paragraph. Electronic reprint actually read: https://file-lianxh.oss-cn-shenzhen.aliyuncs.com/Refs/Spring2024/Athey_2018_Approximate_Residual_Balancing.pdf. Author implementation is stated to be in R package balanceHD, but this contribution does not use an author-code snapshot or commit.

mechanism.name: Average treatment effect in the many-cluster high-dimensional linear design

generation_equations.label: Latent many-cluster centres
generation_equations.expression: For k=1,...,20, c_k ~ Normal_p(0, I_p); centre vectors are mutually independent. p=4000 in the Table 2 reference setting.

generation_equations.label: Individual centre assignment
generation_equations.expression: K_i ~ Uniform{1,...,20}; C_i=c_{K_i}. Cluster labels are drawn independently across individuals conditional on the centre set.

generation_equations.label: Treatment assignment
generation_equations.expression: W_i | K_i=k ~ Bernoulli(eta) for k=1,...,10; W_i | K_i=k ~ Bernoulli(1-eta) for k=11,...,20; eta in {0.1,0.25}.

generation_equations.label: Covariate noise and observed covariates
generation_equations.expression: Z_i ~ Normal_p(0,I_p); X_i=C_i+Z_i. The source writes Z_i~N(0,I_p); explicit cross-individual and cross-variable independence conventions used in the implementation are disclosed in adaptations.

generation_equations.label: Outcome noise
generation_equations.expression: epsilon_i ~ Normal(0,1), so variance=1. Cross-independence from Z, centres and W is an implementation convention not fully enumerated by the source paragraph.

generation_equations.label: Observed outcome
generation_equations.expression: Y_i = X_i^T beta + W_i + epsilon_i, corresponding to the source notation Y_i=(C_i+Z_i) beta + W_i + epsilon_i.

generation_equations.label: Dense beta profile
generation_equations.expression: Raw beta_j proportional to j^(-1/2), j=1,...,p; rescale to ||beta||_2=3.

generation_equations.label: Harmonic beta profile
generation_equations.expression: Raw beta_j proportional to 1/(j+9), j=1,...,p; equivalently (1/10,1/11,...,1/(p+9)); rescale to ||beta||_2=3.

generation_equations.label: Moderately sparse beta profile
generation_equations.expression: Raw beta=(10 repeated 10 times, 1 repeated 90 times, 0 repeated p-100 times); rescale to ||beta||_2=3.

generation_equations.label: Very sparse beta profile
generation_equations.expression: Raw beta=(1 repeated 10 times, 0 repeated p-10 times); rescale to ||beta||_2=3.

generation_equations.label: Potential outcomes and true target
generation_equations.expression: Structural interpretation for w in {0,1}: Y_i(w)=X_i^T beta+w+epsilon_i, so ATE=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=1.

sampling.unit: individual within one simulated dataset; twenty latent cluster centres are generated once per dataset/replication
sampling.dependence: Conditional on the generated centre vectors, individual cluster labels, treatment assignments, covariate noise and outcome errors are sampled independently according to the specified laws. Marginally, rows are dependent because individuals can share randomly generated cluster centres. No interference is added.

assumptions: Consistency: the observed outcome is Y=Y(W).
Potential outcomes are defined by Y(w)=X^T beta + w + epsilon for w in {0,1}; this is the explicit structural interpretation of the paper’s observed outcome equation.

Conditional exchangeability given observed X follows under the implementation convention that epsilon is independent of cluster assignment, treatment randomization and covariate noise; this independence is not fully enumerated in the source paragraph and requires scientific confirmation.

Positivity: for eta in {0.1,0.25}, the treatment probability conditional on latent cluster is eta or 1-eta, hence bounded in [eta, 1-eta]; the marginal propensity conditional on X is a mixture in the same interval.

No interference: one individual’s potential outcome does not depend on other individuals’ treatment assignments. Shared random cluster centres create across-unit dependence in the sampling distribution, not causal interference.

properties.notes: p=4000 with paper Table 2 reference n=800 (p>n). Effective outcome dimension depends on beta_profile: dense and harmonic have 4000 nonzero coefficients; moderately_sparse has 100 (first 10 raw coefficients 10, next 90 raw coefficients 1); very_sparse has 10 (first 10 raw coefficients 1). In each case beta is rescaled to ||beta||_2=3. Covariate dependence/treatment imbalance arises through 20 shared latent Gaussian centres, each c_k~N_p(0,I_p), and cluster-specific treatment probabilities. No interactions or nonlinear outcome terms are present.

estimand.name: ATE = E[Y(1)-Y(0)]
estimand.definition: Superpopulation average effect of the intervention setting W from 0 to 1, holding the pretreatment covariate vector X fixed in the potential outcomes, under the many-cluster DGP. This is a population ATE, not an estimator RMSE or finite-sample treatment-group contrast.

truth.expression: Superpopulation average effect of the intervention setting W from 0 to 1, holding the pretreatment covariate vector X fixed in the potential outcomes, under the many-cluster DGP. This is a population ATE, not an estimator RMSE or finite-sample treatment-group contrast.
truth.derivation: Exact algebraic potential-outcome contrast. For each fixed X and shared epsilon, Y(1)-Y(0)=(X^T beta+1+epsilon)-(X^T beta+epsilon)=1; no numerical integration or Monte Carlo is required.

adaptations: Translate the observed outcome equation Y_i = (C_i + Z_i)^T beta + W_i + epsilon_i into the potential-outcome representation Y_i(w) = X_i^T beta + w + epsilon_i, holding pretreatment X_i and the same additive error fixed, to state the ATE target explicitly.

For executable sampling, treat the individual cluster-label draws, Z_i draws, W_i assignment draws conditional on cluster, and epsilon_i draws as mutually independent where not linked by the specified conditional law. The source paragraph specifies cluster-centre independence and W probabilities by centre group, but does not spell out every cross-variable independence clause; this convention remains pending scientific confirmation.
Represent eta=0.1 and eta=0.25 crossed with the four source beta profiles as eight named scenarios under one mechanism family. Same-family parameter combinations are not separate DGP families.

Use the collection interface generate(config, n, seed) and expose only observed X1..Xp, W and Y. Smoke-check n=128 is a package validation run, not a replacement for the paper Table 2 sample size n=800.
